formats.name: Identity twist reveal ("you've been watching it")
formats.whyItWorks: Opens like a normal organic post the viewer would watch anyway, then reveals in the last third that the post/graphic/caption they just enjoyed was made by the product. The reveal is the payoff, so people watch to the end and replay. Scored 9/10, our best test. Agencies also rate scenario-first openings and a real reaction pause above scripted pitches; the stale pattern is the ring-light testimonial that reads as an ad in 0.5 s.

beats.picture: Actor in a real shop/kitchen, phone selfie framing, holds up phone showing a pretty Instagram post (real screen recording composited)
beats.speech: "Okay, I have to show you this post. It got more comments than anything I've done this year."

beats.picture: Actor scrolls the real BuPulse feed/calendar recording; the post, then two more
beats.speech: "And then my friend asked, who is your designer?" (beat, small laugh)

beats.picture: Cut to real BuPulse screen: calendar with the posts scheduled, logo on the graphics (real capture, no AI screens)
beats.speech: "Nobody. It writes in my brand voice, puts my logo on it, and it's all in one calendar."

beats.picture: Actor back on camera, real reaction face; on-screen text: Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn
beats.speech: "Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, one calendar. I just approve it."

beats.picture: Actor to camera, relaxed
beats.speech: "If you want to see it, comment BUPULSE and we'll send you the link."

formats.look: Phone selfie, slightly off-centre, handheld drift, window light, no ring light; unretouched skin; real screen recordings as inserts; captions white bold with dark outline; room tone, no music bed over speech.
formats.realVsAi: Real: every screen, logo, graphic, post, calendar, the reveal facts. AI-ok: the first-frame actor still then animated, room B-roll. Voice: real recorded Kinyarwanda/English, never AI Kinyarwanda.
formats.bupulseExample: Shop owner shows a post that got attention, then reveals BuPulse wrote it in her brand voice and designed it with her logo, scheduled from one calendar to Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn.
formats.cta: Comment BUPULSE and we'll send you the link.

formats.name: Loop story (end flows back into the first frame)
formats.whyItWorks: The last line completes the first sentence, so the video replays without the viewer noticing, which lifts watch time and replays. Scored 8/10. East African top performers are also 5-6 s loops and calm one-take tours (2.9M views on a 6 s loop in our library).

beats.picture: Actor mid-action in kitchen/shop, already talking, unboxing a stack of printed flyers vs a phone
beats.speech: "...and that's the reason I stopped doing my posts at midnight."

beats.picture: Cut to her old routine: phone notes, blank screen, tired face (real, acted); on-screen: 'Sunday 11 pm'
beats.speech: "Every Sunday I'd sit with a blank page, what do I even post this week."

beats.picture: Real BuPulse Autopilot screen recording: the week planned, one tap approve
beats.speech: "Now Autopilot plans the week and I approve it with one tap."

beats.picture: Actor relaxed, shows phone with Monday's posts scheduled (real capture insert)
beats.speech: "Posts go out to Instagram and Facebook by themselves, in my voice."

beats.picture: Actor turns to the camera; the frame matches the first frame
beats.speech: "Save this for the next time it's midnight, and..." (cuts to 0:00 line)

formats.look: Single location, one handheld take plus two inserts; the last frame matches the first (same crop, same light); no intro card; caption text same position throughout.
formats.realVsAi: Real: Autopilot screens and the approve tap. AI-ok: first-frame actor and room, the 'old routine' B-roll. Real human voice only.
formats.bupulseExample: Owner stops doing posts at midnight; Autopilot plans the week, one-tap approve; ends mid-sentence that connects to the opening line.

formats.name: Split-screen reveal (reaction on top, real screen below)
formats.whyItWorks: Top half is a person reacting, bottom half is the real screen doing the work. The viewer sees proof and a human reaction at once. Scored 8/10. Arcads' own tooling and our research confirm the standard pattern for digital products: real UI capture plus a separate actor, composited in the edit, because video models draw screens as gibberish.

beats.picture: Split: actor top (jaw-drop, phone-framed), bottom shows a real blank calendar; text 'My week of posts. 30 seconds.'
beats.speech: "Watch this. I'm not touching anything."

beats.picture: Bottom: real BuPulse screen recording: Autopilot generating the week; top: actor reacting naturally
beats.speech: "It's writing the captions... in my brand voice."

beats.picture: Bottom: graphics appear with the logo; top: actor points at screen
beats.speech: "And it designs the graphics with my logo on them."

beats.picture: Bottom: tap Approve; calendar fills Instagram/Facebook/LinkedIn
beats.speech: "One tap. That's the whole week, three platforms."

beats.picture: Full-frame actor
beats.speech: "Want one? Request a quote and we'll set it up."

formats.look: 9:16, 50/50 split, thin divider; actor in phone-selfie framing with imperfect crop; real captures at native resolution (letterbox 'fit' on blurred fill); captions in the actor half's lower third.
formats.realVsAi: Real: the whole bottom half. AI-ok: top actor (first frame then animate). Real recorded voice.
formats.bupulseExample: Actor reacts while the real Autopilot week plans itself and one tap approves it.

formats.name: 60-second challenge
formats.whyItWorks: A visible clock gives a built-in hook and stakes ('can I do a week of posts in 60 seconds'). Scored 7/10: strong retention but it needs tight editing, and the clock must be honest.

beats.picture: Phone on a table, a real timer 01:00 on screen, actor leans in
beats.speech: "One minute. A full week of posts for my shop. Go."

beats.picture: Screen recording with timer visible: write posts in brand voice
beats.speech: "First, the captions, in my voice."

beats.picture: Screen: graphics with logo generated; timer at 0:30
beats.speech: "Now the graphics, my logo, my colours."

beats.picture: Screen: schedule to Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn; timer stops
beats.speech: "Scheduled. Time check..." (show true timer)

beats.picture: Actor shows timer, shrugs
beats.speech: "Comment AD and we'll DM you how."

formats.look: Visible real timer overlay (do not fake the time; speed-ramp is ok if labeled 'sped up'); handheld phone over-the-shoulder shots; natural light.
formats.realVsAi: Real: timer and screen work, actual elapsed time disclosed. AI-ok: actor opening frame only.
formats.bupulseExample: Race the clock to plan, design and schedule a week of posts with BuPulse; disclose any speed-up.
formats.cta: Comment AD and we'll DM you.

formats.name: Selfie 'things I wish I knew' (store-owner shows)
formats.whyItWorks: First-person, mistake-based list that feels like advice from a peer, not an ad: scenario/diagnostic hooks and third-person social proof beat 'this changed my life'. Selfie testimonial scored 6-7/10 in our tests, our weakest, so use it for volume, not as the lead creative.

beats.picture: Selfie, walking in her shop, text '3 things I wish I knew about posting'
beats.speech: "Three things I wish somebody told me about posting for my shop."

beats.picture: Actor to camera, text '1. Post at lunch'; cut to real calendar insert
beats.speech: "One: be consistent. Mine was random, now it's one calendar."

beats.picture: Text '2. Same voice every time'; real post-writing screen
beats.speech: "Two: sound like you. It writes in my brand voice."

beats.picture: Text '3. Don't skip leads'; real website chat saving a lead
beats.speech: "Three: the website chat saves leads while I'm busy."

beats.picture: Selfie close
beats.speech: "Save this, and tap the link in bio if you want it."

formats.look: Phone selfie handheld, walking, real background noise, ticked-list text top third; no polished lighting.
formats.realVsAi: Real: all screens. AI-ok: actor and shop first frame. No fabricated testimonial numbers or reviews.
formats.bupulseExample: Three tips: consistency (one calendar), same voice (brand voice), no lost leads (website chat saves them), Kinyarwanda version as a variant.
formats.cta: Save this, tap the link in bio.

do: Cast an ordinary adult with specific age, build, short natural hair or braids, not model-perfect
Real skin from light, not texture: soft side light, warm undertones, natural sheen on forehead, nose and cheekbones; never ask for pores, blemishes or grain (13 Nov 2026, Higgsfield comparison)
Exact wardrobe: 'faded green t-shirt with a small stain, plain cap, simple earrings'
Real Kigali settings: tin-roofed shop, red dust, motorbikes, plastic chairs, wall posters, mixed clutter
Soft natural window daylight, mixed light, slightly warm, slightly overexposed highlights
'iPhone front camera selfie, one-hand, slightly shaky, autofocus micro-pulses, no stabilization' (Higgsfield Sora 2 guide)
Asymmetric framing, partly cut-off head, off-centre subject, occasional soft focus
Natural gestures, blinks, glances away, small laughs, mid-sentence start
Generate first frame as a still, approve it, then animate it
Keep the face identical by pinning one avatar/reference image across clips
Prompt for ethnicity and place as facts: 'Rwandan woman in her 30s, Kigali market'
Record real Kinyarwanda voice with a real person; use captions
dont: No symmetrical centered face with glossy skin and a blurred perfect bokeh background
No airbrushed teeth, uniform smile, plastic hair, identical twin faces across clips
No clean empty rooms and spotless kitchens; no logos/text drawn by the model
No AI-drawn screens or UI; use real recordings only
No stock-photo African clothing/props or generic 'Africa' backgrounds; use actual local items
No 12-s pure talking head with no cuts, no breathing, no pause
No AI Kinyarwanda voice or lip-sync
No fake reviews, fake stats or fake before/afters
Negatives to paste: 'no beauty filter, no smoothing, no watermark, no extra fingers, no warped text, no studio backdrop, no stock look'
